questions.question: In which of these do you write a program by typing lines of text?
questions.options: A flowchart | A storyboard | Python | Scratch
questions.explanation: Python is a text-based language — you type each instruction. Scratch uses blocks you snap together instead.
questions.sourceUnitTitle: Block It Out: Moving from Blocks to Text

questions.question: In Python, what does the line score = 10 do?
questions.options: Checks whether score equals 10 | Stores the value 10 in a variable called score | Prints the word score ten times | Deletes the variable score
questions.correctAnswer: Stores the value 10 in a variable called score
questions.explanation: A single = puts a value into a variable. So score = 10 stores 10 in the box called score.
questions.sourceUnitTitle: Block It Out: Moving from Blocks to Text

questions.question: Inside a Python if statement, which symbol asks whether two values are equal?
questions.explanation: Double equals (==) compares two values to see if they match. A single = stores a value instead.
questions.sourceUnitTitle: Block It Out: Moving from Blocks to Text

questions.question: What is an IDE, such as Thonny or IDLE?
questions.options: A folder where photos are stored | A type of printer for code | A program that helps you write, test and run code | A cable that connects a computer to the internet
questions.correctAnswer: A program that helps you write, test and run code
questions.explanation: An IDE (Integrated Development Environment) is your coding workshop — you write, save, test and run your programs inside it.
questions.sourceUnitTitle: Block It Out: Moving from Blocks to Text

questions.question: Layla must build a quiz game. First she splits the job into three smaller parts: ask questions, check answers, and show the score. What is this skill called?
questions.options: Decomposition | Debugging | Formatting | Encryption
questions.explanation: Decomposition means breaking a big problem into smaller parts you can solve one at a time — exactly what Layla did.
questions.sourceUnitTitle: Decomposing Problems: Creating a Smart Solution

questions.question: In a micro:bit Python program, what does sleep(2000) do?
questions.options: Pauses the program for 2 seconds | Repeats the next line 2000 times | Makes the screen twice as bright | Turns the micro:bit off for 2000 minutes
questions.explanation: sleep counts in milliseconds, and 2000 milliseconds is 2 seconds — so the program waits for 2 seconds before the next step.
questions.sourceUnitTitle: Decomposing Problems: Creating a Smart Solution

questions.question: Omar has no micro:bit at home, but he still tests his program in a simulator. Why is a simulator useful?
questions.options: It charges the battery faster | It types the code for you | It makes any program run with no bugs | It behaves like the real device, so you can test your code safely without one
questions.correctAnswer: It behaves like the real device, so you can test your code safely without one
questions.explanation: A simulator is software that acts like the real device. You can try your program, watch what happens and fix mistakes before using real hardware.
questions.sourceUnitTitle: Decomposing Problems: Creating a Smart Solution

questions.question: Before writing any code, Sagal writes her plan as an exact, ordered list of steps. What is this plan called?
questions.options: A password | An algorithm | A spreadsheet | A domain name
questions.explanation: An algorithm is a precise, step-by-step plan. Writing it first makes the code much easier to build and debug.
questions.sourceUnitTitle: Decomposing Problems: Creating a Smart Solution

questions.question: Hodan wants to connect wireless headphones to the phone in her pocket. Which connection is designed for exactly that short distance?
questions.options: Bluetooth | An Ethernet cable | A fibre-optic cable | A satellite link
questions.explanation: Bluetooth is made for short-range wireless links between nearby devices, like headphones and a phone.
questions.sourceUnitTitle: Connections Are Made: Accessing the Internet

questions.question: In the web address https://www.school.org, which part is the top-level domain (TLD)?
questions.options: www | .org | https | school
questions.explanation: The TLD is the ending of the address. Here it is .org; other common ones are .com and .net.
questions.sourceUnitTitle: Connections Are Made: Accessing the Internet

questions.question: Zahra types the phrase how do plants grow in dry places into a search engine. What does the search engine mainly use to find pages?
questions.options: The keywords in her phrase | The colour of her screen | The time of day | Her password
questions.explanation: A search engine picks out the important keywords — like plants, grow and dry — and finds pages that match them.
questions.sourceUnitTitle: Connections Are Made: Accessing the Internet

questions.question: A website asks for your full name, home address and school before it lets you play a game. What should you do?
questions.options: Type it in quickly so you can start playing | Post your address in the game chat | Stop and ask a trusted adult before sharing any personal information | Share a friend’s details instead of your own
questions.correctAnswer: Stop and ask a trusted adult before sharing any personal information
questions.explanation: Your name, address and school are personal information. Keep them private, and always check with a trusted adult before sharing anything online.
questions.sourceUnitTitle: Connections Are Made: Accessing the Internet

questions.question: What is a data model?
questions.options: A kind of printer | A game controller | A photograph of a computer | A computer representation of a real-life situation
questions.correctAnswer: A computer representation of a real-life situation
questions.explanation: A data model uses numbers and formulas inside a computer to stand for something real, like a shop’s sales or tomorrow’s weather.
questions.sourceUnitTitle: The Power of Data: Using Data Modelling

questions.question: In a spreadsheet, what is the address of the cell in column B, row 3?
questions.options: 3B | B-3-cell | B3 | 33
questions.explanation: A cell address is its column letter followed by its row number — column B, row 3 is cell B3.
questions.sourceUnitTitle: The Power of Data: Using Data Modelling

questions.question: A shop records each day’s sales in cells A1 to A7 of a spreadsheet. Which formula adds up the whole week?
questions.options: ADD(A1-A7) | =TOTAL A1;A7 | =SUM(A1:A7) | SUM A1 to A7
questions.explanation: A formula starts with = and SUM(A1:A7) adds every cell from A1 down to A7 — the whole week in one step.
questions.sourceUnitTitle: The Power of Data: Using Data Modelling

questions.question: A tablet needs one special piece of software running before any apps can work. Which is it?
questions.options: The operating system | A racing game | A drawing app | A photo filter
questions.explanation: The operating system is systems software — it runs the whole device and lets all the other apps work on top of it.

questions.question: A bit is a single 0 or 1. How many bits make one byte?
questions.explanation: One byte is 8 bits. Bigger units like kilobytes and megabytes are built from bytes.

questions.question: An AND gate gives an output of 1 only when:
questions.options: both of its inputs are 1 | it is switched off | either one of its inputs is 1 | both of its inputs are 0
questions.explanation: That is the AND rule: the output is 1 only if the first input AND the second input are both 1.

questions.question: Computers store every kind of data — words, pictures and sound — using which two digits?
questions.options: 5 and 10 | 1 and 2 | 0 and 1 | 0 and 9
questions.explanation: All digital data is stored in binary, which uses only the digits 0 and 1.

questions.question: A breakfast program must show the step crack the egg before stir the egg. What do we call the exact order of instructions in a program?
questions.options: A sequence | A network | A pixel | A password
questions.explanation: A sequence is the specific order of instructions. A computer follows the steps strictly in that order.

questions.question: On a micro:bit, each LED’s brightness is a number from 0 to 9. What does a brightness of 0 mean?
questions.options: The LED turns red | The LED is off | The LED is at full brightness | The LED flashes forever
questions.explanation: 0 means off and 9 means full brightness — the numbers in between are dimmer levels of light.

questions.question: Amal notices her light show repeats the same four steps again and again, so she writes one loop instead of twenty lines. Which skill did she use to spot this?
questions.options: Encryption | Downloading | Formatting | Pattern recognition
questions.explanation: Pattern recognition means looking for a repeating pattern and using it to solve a problem — like turning repeated steps into one loop.

questions.question: A game keeps track of lives: the player starts with 3 and the number changes while playing. What should the programmer store the number of lives in?
questions.options: A cable | A printer | A comment | A variable
questions.explanation: A variable is a named box that stores a value that can change — perfect for a score or a number of lives.

questions.question: A dice game shows a different number each time, and nobody can guess it in advance. In programming, what do we call an outcome you cannot predict?
questions.options: Sorted | Saved | Constant | Random
questions.explanation: Random means an outcome you cannot predict. Programs use random numbers to make games fair and surprising.

questions.question: Warsame measures the temperature of water as it cools. Why is temperature called continuous data?
questions.options: It is always a whole number | It never changes at all | It can take any value in a range, including in-between values | It can only ever be Yes or No
questions.correctAnswer: It can take any value in a range, including in-between values
questions.explanation: Continuous data can be any value in a range — the water can be 21 degrees, 20.5 degrees, or anything in between.

questions.question: In a class database, all the information about one pupil sits together in one row. What is that row of related information called?
questions.options: A record | A pixel | A field | A password
questions.explanation: One row about one person or thing is a record. Each single piece of information inside it, like a name or age, is a field.

questions.question: What is the job of a server on a network?
questions.options: To provide data and services to other computers | To charge the batteries of laptops | To print every document twice | To block all messages on the network
questions.correctAnswer: To provide data and services to other computers
questions.explanation: A server serves! It is a computer that provides data and services — like web pages or files — to the other devices that ask for them.

questions.question: Fatima’s message is scrambled on its journey so that only the right person can unscramble and read it. What is this protection called?
questions.options: Printing | Deletion | Charging | Encryption
questions.explanation: Encryption scrambles a message so only the right people can read it. It keeps information safe as it travels across a network.

questions.question: Analogue data, like the sound of a voice in the air, is best described as:
questions.options: a smooth signal that changes continuously | a signal made only of 0s and 1s | a printed page of numbers | a kind of computer keyboard
questions.correctAnswer: a smooth signal that changes continuously
questions.explanation: Analogue data flows smoothly, like a voice or a dimming light. Digital data is different — it is made of separate 0s and 1s.

questions.question: A robot in a factory paints cars all day, every day, without making mistakes. What makes it able to do this?
questions.options: It gets bored but hides it well | It follows a program that people wrote for it | It thinks exactly like a human does | It works without any instructions at all
questions.correctAnswer: It follows a program that people wrote for it
questions.explanation: A robot is a machine we can program. It repeats its instructions exactly, which is why it is so good at doing the same job all day.

questions.question: Before building her program, Nimo writes a list of everything it must do to count as a success. When the finished program does everything on that list, we say it meets its:
questions.options: file size | success criteria | screen resolution | download speed
questions.explanation: Success criteria are the list of things a program must do to be a success. Ticking them off shows your program really works.

questions.question: Aisha types 2+3 into a spreadsheet cell, but the computer does not work out the answer. Which symbol must every spreadsheet formula begin with?
questions.explanation: A formula must start with an equals sign. Typing =2+3 tells the spreadsheet to calculate, so the cell shows 5.

questions.question: In Khadra’s house, one box shares the internet with every phone and laptop in the family. Which device is it?
questions.options: A monitor | A router | A speaker | A mouse
questions.explanation: A router connects a home network to the internet and passes messages to every device in the house.

questions.question: In Scratch, what does a repeat loop do with the blocks placed inside it?
questions.options: Deletes them from the project | Changes their colour once | Runs them again and again | Emails them to a friend
questions.explanation: A repeat loop runs the blocks inside it over and over — that is how one short script can make a character dance many times.

questions.question: In a Caesar cipher with a key of 3, the letter A becomes D and B becomes E. What does C become?
questions.options: F | G | E | Z
questions.explanation: A key of 3 shifts every letter three places along the alphabet: C moves past D and E to become F.

questions.question: Which of these is hardware — a part of a computer you can actually touch?
questions.options: A game’s instructions | The keyboard | An app’s code | A saved story file
questions.explanation: Hardware is the physical parts you can touch, like a keyboard or screen. Software is the programs and instructions, which you cannot touch.
